messages:
Aaron: Noticed a recurring throughput dip during nightly backups (02:15-03:00 UTC) for the last 5 days. Throughput SLO for /v1/stream is burning ~4%/day. Root cause looks like IO saturation on the serving pod disks, not a model or network issue.
Mei: Confirmed on my side. iostat shows spike in await ~120ms on a couple of nodes, pods get CPU-steal and request queue grows.
Javier: Can you drop the 1h chart? I want to compare request processing time vs loopback IO waits.
Aaron: https://dash.redwood/internal/slo/throughput?range=5d — attaching quick image in thread.
Noor: If the backups are colliding with peak maintenance tasks we should move backups to a maintenance window or throttle them. Also thinking: we should split the throughput SLO into two buckets (interactive vs background-heavy routes) to reduce noisy neighbor effects.
Mei: Agree. Short-term mitigation: 1) mark backup jobs as low-IO with ionice nice, 2) move one backup shard to a different AZ, 3) pin affected disks to newer firmware. I can do 1+2 tonight. ETA 12h.
Javier: I'll own dashboarding and alerting changes. Tasks: add a per-AZ throughput heatmap, per-route 10/50/95/99 percentiles, and an alert if sustained drop >20% for 10m. ETA 24h.
Noor: For SLO decision: we shouldn't rebaseline immediately. Proposed approach: keep current SLO, allocate a temporary error budget credit to affected route owners (internal bookkeeping), and run a 7-day experiment after mitigations before we consider rebaseline.
Aaron: Sounds good. Add to postmortem action tracker and list owners + verification steps. Verification should be: 7-day rolling throughput variance <5% and error budget burn <0.5%/day.
autoscale-bot: Autoscaler notice: scaling cooldowns paused for cluster-clone-7 due to ongoing maintenance window.
Mei: Adding runbook step to throttle non-critical replica syncs during 02:00-04:00 UTC. Diff of runbook change (snippet):
```
- cron: "0 2 * * *" backup.sh
+ cron: "15 3 * * *" backup.sh # moved to avoid serving peak
```
Javier: Dashboard PromQL for per-AZ throughput (draft):
```
sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/stream",az=~"us-.*"}[5m])) by (az)
```
Noor: Action items (compact):
- MEI-502: implement ionice + shard move (owner: Mei) ETA 12h
- JAV-403: update dashboards + alert rules (owner: Javier) ETA 24h
- AAR-210: postmortem tracker entry + customer comms draft (owner: Aaron) ETA 48h
- OPS-711: disk firmware roll plan (owner: Infra) ETA 72h
Metrics-bot: Scheduled job `throughput_regression_check` will run hourly and post deltas to /reports/throughput-deltas.
Aaron: Also: Noor, please create the internal temporary error budget credit entry and communicate to route owners. We should log the credit id in the tracker.
Noor: Will do. Creating credit: CREDIT-2026-03-24-1, recording in tracker.
Javier: Small test plan for validation: run a synthetic throughput workload for 30m after ionice + shard move and verify 95th latency and throughput restored. I can run it at 03:30 UTC tomorrow. Need a second to observe.
Mei: I'll be on-call and run the ops steps, available at 03:00-04:30 UTC.
Aaron: Great. Meeting: reconvene in 7 days (2026-03-31 14:00 UTC) for follow-up postmortem and SLO decision (keep vs rebaseline). Everyone, update the tracker when tasks complete.
Noor: One more note: if disk firmware pack fails we may have to route traffic away from affected azs temporarily — adding that contingency to the runbook.
Mei: Quick logs where IO waits spike:
```
2026-03-22T02:23:11Z pod-7 kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
2026-03-22T02:23:12Z pod-7 iostat: Device: nvme0n1 tps=320 await=118.32
```
Aaron: Thanks team. Recap in tracker + assign timeline. We'll keep SLO untouched for now and use the error budget credit + mitigations. :thumbsup:
